ruleTitle: Protect Homepage Brand Authority & Legal SRA Triage Hub
constraintDescription: The Homepage (/) is strictly locked as the Brand Authority & Legal SRA Triage Hub (Title: 'Settlement Agreement Checker & SRA Triage UK | SettlementCheck', H1: 'Settlement Agreement Checker & Legal SRA Triage Hub UK'). Strictly prohibit assigning 'Settlement Agreement Calculator' to /; the commercial calculator intent belongs exclusively to /calculator/.

ruleTitle: Protect Main Calculator Sole Commercial Transactional Tool
constraintDescription: Preserve /calculator/ as the Sole Commercial Transactional Tool (Title: 'Settlement Agreement Calculator UK (2026/27) | SettlementCheck', H1: 'Free Employee Settlement Agreement Calculator UK (2026 Rates)'). Never replace the <title> with informational 'How to...' phrasing.

ruleTitle: Anti-Churn Title Freeze (SERP Pixel & CTR Calibrated Protection)
constraintDescription: Forbid cosmetic title rewrites when an existing page title is already CTR-calibrated and within 50-60 characters / SERP pixel budgets. Reject cosmetic title rewrites and downgrade actuationScope to ADDITIVE_CONTENT_AND_LINKS.

ruleTitle: ITEPA 2003 s.403 & s.402D PENP Statutory Precision
constraintDescription: Never use promissory phrasing like 'You can expect up to £30,000 tax-free'. Always state that genuine non-contractual compensation up to £30,000 can be paid tax-free under s.403 ITEPA 2003, whereas contractual PILON and Post-Employment Notice Pay (s.402D) remain subject to income tax and National Insurance.

ruleTitle: SRA, FCA, CMA & 5 Adversarial Legal Traps Compliance
constraintDescription: Use strictly descriptive phrasing (never prescriptive imperatives like 'Do not sign', 'Do not accept', 'You should ask for', or 'What to say to your employer'). Clarify that ACAS Code 4 (10 calendar days) is statutory guidance rather than an irrevocable right (Routledge v Grant), that s.111A applies only to ordinary unfair dismissal, and that employers standardly provide a capped contribution (typically £350 to £500+ +VAT) upon agreement completion as a commercial practice rather than a statutory obligation under Section 203.
prohibitedPhrases: what to say to your employer
legally required to pay your legal fees
